title: Coarse-graining
summary: A many-to-one map from fine states to a smaller set of macro-descriptions, intentionally discarding distinctions.

context.note: Framework is named textually in this seed release; full recursive first-principles closure remains future work.

assumptions.text: Fine state space X, macrostate space Y, and map C:X→Y are specified.

content.plain: Coarse-graining keeps distinctions relevant at one scale or task and merges others.
content.exact: A coarse-graining can be represented by a non-injective map C:X→Y. States x1≠x2 with C(x1)=C(x2) are indistinguishable at the coarse level.
content.example: Block averaging maps many high-resolution samples to fewer averages.
content.caveat: Coarse-graining is not automatically intelligent or optimal. Whether discarded information is nuisance depends on an objective, observer, model, and scale.

relations.note: Preimages of macro-values form groups of fine states.
A chosen coarse-graining can suppress variation treated as noise.
Repeated coarse-grainings can define multiple scales.

verification.method: QEVA seed formulation checked editorially for mathematical coherence; no external formal proof artifact is claimed.
